profile.summary: iliakan is a senior JavaScript developer with deep expertise in jQuery's core internals, specializing in memory leak fixes, legacy browser compatibility (particularly IE6-8), and DOM optimization. Their contributions focus on resolving long-standing bugs related to DOM node lifecycle, event handling, and performance degradation in older browsers. The developer demonstrates strong problem-solving skills in debugging memory leaks, conditional browser logic, and performance tuning for legacy environments. While their work is confined to jQuery and legacy JavaScript, their technical depth in these areas suggests significant experience with low-level JavaScript behavior and browser quirks.
skill_evidence: "wrapAll creates an intermediate node then clones it. The intermediate node leaks. Removed cloning for a string thus fixing the bug." (DOM node cloning leak)
"Repairs long-standing bug about incorrect behavior of submit bubbling in all IEs." (IE-specific event handling fix)
"unload cleanup is called on IE7, IE8, but should be only on IE6" (Legacy browser conditional logic)
"The conditional comment is the most reliable way to sniff the memory leak feature." (Conditional comment usage)
"No need to load CPU on newer browsers with cleaning stuff." (Performance optimization)
"I'd prefer also remove unneeded expando/cache pollution from $.data if asking for data, not setting it." (jQuery internals optimization)
"Only IE6 does [the leak]." (IE6-specific memory leak identification)
